statement: The Football Association of Montenegro was admitted to FIFA membership at the FIFA Congress in Zurich on 31 May 2007 (57th Congress; 208th member).
limitations: Four non-FIFA sources (the FA itself, a contemporaneous wire report, a Xinhua report and a memoir account) agree on the day; the Xinhua report shows admission was scheduled for the Congress day, not earlier. FIFA primary (Congress minutes/circular) still pending; year consistent with AGB2-E010 (2007).

statement: SAFA's FIFA membership was reinstated at the FIFA Congress in Zurich on 3 July 1992, after the earlier expulsion era.
limitations: Two independent sources agree on the day; UPI is a contemporaneous report of the Congress itself. Still not a FIFA primary document; year consistent with AGB2-E010 (1992).

statement: UEFA's official history states the LFF was readmitted to FIFA on 9 December 1991.
limitations: Conflicts with AGB2-C004 (FIFA report year 1992) and AGB2-C005 (UPI: Lithuania among members accepted at the 3 July 1992 Congress). The semantics (ExCo readmission later confirmed by Congress, or different events) are not established.

statement: The FIFA Financial Report 2018 records Lithuania's affiliation years as 1923/1992.
limitations: Year-level; conflicts with AGB2-C003 and is coarse relative to AGB2-C005.

statement: At the FIFA Congress in Zurich on Friday 3 July 1992, 14 nations were accepted as members; the report names Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Russia, Armenia, Belarus, Georgia, Ukraine, South Africa, Croatia, Slovenia and St. Kitts and Nevis (12 of the 14 named), and states the three Baltic states had previously been FIFA members until 1940.
limitations: Contemporaneous wire report of the Congress; not a FIFA document; the two unnamed members of the 14 are not identified. Consistent with the 1992 affiliation years of the named teams in AGB2-E010.

statement: As of the 3 July 1992 Congress, the applications of Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kirghizia (Kyrgyzstan), Moldova, Uzbekistan, Tadzhikistan (Tajikistan) and Turkmenistan had been postponed; the Congress left the decision to the Executive Committee at a December meeting, so these seven were not FIFA members on 3 July 1992.
limitations: Establishes non-membership only at the Congress date; it does not establish when membership later began (the FIFA report gives 1994 for all seven; the ExCo 'December meeting' outcome is not evidenced in this batch).

statement: The DFV applied for FIFA membership on 6 February 1951, was accepted as a provisional member on 6 October 1951 and as a full member on 24 July 1952.
limitations: Encyclopedic secondary source only; no FIFA primary record. The German DR does not appear in the 2018 affiliation-year list.

statement: The DFV ceased to be a separate FIFA member in 1990 in connection with German reunification and the merger of the DFV into the DFB; the exact exit date is not established by available sources (last GDR international was played 12 September 1990; reunification followed on 3 October 1990).
limitations: Deliberately no day-level date: the source links the merger to reunification 'in 1990' but does not state a FIFA membership end date. Replaces batch01 AGB1-C012, which wrongly used the national unification day as the exit day (see AGB2-XR06).

statement: The PFA was affiliated to FIFA as a full member at the 51st Ordinary Congress in Paris on 8 June 1998; from May 1995 it held provisional membership restricted to friendly matches played in the territory of another FIFA-affiliated association.
limitations: Non-FIFA research source; consistent with the 1998 affiliation year in AGB2-E010. Whether the May 1995 provisional status would or would not make matches eligible is a policy question for the mainline; this batch does not decide it.

statement: A Wikipedia-mirror account states that on 13 October 1979 the FIFA Executive Committee passed a resolution readmitting the CFA as a member.
limitations: Search-excerpt-only evidence; page could not be obtained (anti-bot) in either batch. The relation between this decision date and the effective membership date is explicitly unresolved (see AGB2-C011/C012).

statement: A Wikipedia-mirror account states that on 7 July 1980 the 42nd FIFA Congress approved the Executive Committee's decision restoring the CFA's lawful rights in FIFA.
limitations: Search-excerpt-only evidence. Whether membership took effect with the 1979 ExCo decision or with the 1980 Congress approval is not established; the single target match group before 1980-07-07 remains unresolved.

statement: A Xinhua retrospective states China rejoined FIFA in 1980, after Havelange's August 1979 visit to negotiate membership.
limitations: Year-level only; consistent with AGB2-E010 (China PR 1931/1980) and with AGB2-C011; does not settle the exact day.

statement: At the 49th FIFA Congress on 16 June 1994 the Congress unanimously admitted 14 new member associations, including the Czech Republic and Slovakia and seven former-Soviet republics (the seven are not enumerated in the source).
limitations: Contemporaneous press report, not a FIFA primary record; the dispatch does not enumerate the 14 members. See AGB2-C015 for the bounded identification of the seven.

statement: At the 49th FIFA Congress on 16 June 1994 the Congress rejected the Bosnia and Herzegovina association's membership application, so it was not a FIFA member as of that date.
limitations: Press report of the Congress decision; supports non-membership up to 16 June 1994 only.

statement: Inference across two independent contemporaneous reports (not stated in either alone): the seven former-Soviet republics whose applications were postponed on 3 July 1992 (AGB2-C006: Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan) are the same 'seven former-Soviet republics' the 49th Congress admitted on 16 June 1994 (AGB2-C013); the FIFA report gives all seven affiliation year 1994.
limitations: This is an explicit cross-source inference, not a FIFA enumeration; an earlier ExCo admission for any of the seven is not excluded by these sources. North Macedonia is not mentioned in either report and is not part of this inference.

statement: The BHFF became a full member of FIFA in 1996 (year-level; official strategy timeline), after applying in 1992 and being rejected on 16 June 1994.
limitations: Year-level only; no exact admission day; PDF text extraction failed (image timeline), fact read from search excerpt of the official document.

statement: The FIFA Financial Report 2018 records the Czech Republic's affiliation years as 1907/1994.
limitations: Year-level observation.

statement: The FIFA Financial Report 2018 records Slovakia's affiliation year as 1994.
limitations: Year-level observation.

statement: The FIFA Financial Report 2018 records FYR Macedonia's affiliation year as 1994.
limitations: Year-level only. North Macedonia is not named in either the 3 July 1992 Congress report (AGB2-E011) or the 16 June 1994 dispatch enumeration (AGB2-E006); an unverified online claim of 1993-08-15 exists and is not registered as evidence.

statement: UEFA's official timeline states the NZS joined FIFA in 1992 ('a year earlier' than its 1993 UEFA admission).
limitations: Year-level official account; consistent with the UPI Congress report.

statement: Per the contemporaneous UPI report, Slovenia was among the members accepted at the FIFA Congress on 3 July 1992; Slovenia's international debut (3 June 1992) preceded that date. An unverified mirror claim of 24 November 1992 exists but is not registered as evidence.
limitations: Day-level date rests on a wire report, not a FIFA document; the 24 November 1992 alternative appeared only in low-quality mirror texts (not saved). FIFA primary confirmation needed.
